title: The Hidden Life of Trees: What They Feel, How They Communicate – Discoveries from a Secret World
author: Peter Wohlleben
edition_analyzed: English translation by Jane Billinghurst, published 2016
target_audience: General readers interested in science and natural history
core_themes: Communication and cooperation within forest ecosystems
Interdependence between trees and other species
Human impact on forests and conservation
primary_purpose: To reveal the intricate and often hidden ways that trees interact, communicate, and support one another, challenging conventional perceptions and fostering deeper appreciation and respect for forests.

structure_format.narrative_style: Accessible, anecdotal, and occasionally lyrical; blends storytelling with scientific research
structure_format.organization: Divided into short chapters, each highlighting a different aspect of tree biology or forest interaction
features: Metaphors relating tree behavior to human communities

key_concepts_lessons: Trees communicate through chemical signals and underground fungal networks ('Wood Wide Web').
Trees cooperate by sharing nutrients and warning each other about threats.
Old and young trees engage in complex support systems for the health of the forest.
Forests are resilient, interconnected, and function more like superorganisms than collections of individuals.
Human activities can disrupt the subtle balance of forest ecosystems.
notable_features: Draws on decades of practical forestry experience
Presents advanced scientific ideas in an accessible manner
Blurs lines between popular science and poetic reflection
Promotes empathy and ethical consideration for trees
cultural_historical_context: Published in Germany in 2015 during a period of growing global environmental awareness and climate concern, the book provided a fresh, lay-friendly perspective on forests and quickly became an international bestseller.
reception_impact: International bestseller, translated into multiple languages
Sparked widespread public interest in tree communication and forest ecology
Lauded for making complex science accessible and engaging
Criticized by some scientists for anthropomorphizing trees
comparable_titles: Braiding Sweetgrass by Robin Wall Kimmerer
The Overstory by Richard Powers (though a novel, thematically similar)
The Secret Life of Plants by Peter Tompkins and Christopher Bird
